plain: A person who sits close to an investment team and explains its strategy to clients in depth. Also called a product specialist or investment specialist.
technical: Represents the strategy in pitches, reviews and due-diligence meetings and answers detailed portfolio questions. Does not usually make the buy and sell decisions, which stay with the portfolio managers.
why_it_matters: Coverage teams bring a client portfolio manager into a meeting when the questions go beyond what a salesperson or relationship manager should answer.

expansion: Goldman Sachs's name for its final-round interviews
plain: The last stage of campus recruitment: a series of interviews with people from the business.
technical: Goldman says it typically holds between two and five interviews for campus hires, depending on the division.
why_it_matters: It is the stage at which you meet members of a specific team.

expansion: Working title used outside the United States for the Vice President level
plain: The same level of seniority as Vice President, under a different name.
technical: Goldman listings titled Executive Director carry the corporate title Vice President, and the firm announces one combined Vice President and Executive Director class.
why_it_matters: It is one rung, not two. Do not assume an Executive Director outranks a Vice President.

expansion: Goldman Sachs Asset Management's multi-asset investing group
plain: The investment group that builds and runs whole portfolios across asset classes, including outsourced (OCIO) mandates.
technical: An investing group, separate from the sales organisation. Its OCIO teams work with sales and client relationship professionals.
why_it_matters: OCIO clients are served by this group, so not every client-facing person sits in the Client Solutions Group.
